'''''Leptospermum squarrosum''''', commonly known as the '''peach blossom tea-tree''',<ref name="RBGS">{{cite web |title=''Leptospermum squarrosum'' |url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Leptospermum~squarrosum |publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Sydney |accessdate=11 June 2020}}</ref> is an upright shrub of the family [[Myrtaceae]] and is [[Endemism|endemic]] to central eastern [[New South Wales]]. It has thin, firm bark, broadly lance-shaped to elliptical leaves, relatively large white or pink flowers and fruit that remain on the plant when mature.

==Description==
''Leptospermum squarrosum'' is an erect shrub of variable habit, growing to a height of less than {{cvt|1|m}} to {{cvt|4|m}} or more and has thin, firm bark. Young stem are silky-hairy at first, soon [[wikt:glabrous|glabrous]]. The leaves are variable but mostly broadly lance-shaped to elliptical, {{cvt|5–15|mm}} long and {{cvt|2–5|mm}} wide with a sharply-pointed tip and tapering to a short [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]]. The flowers are white or pink, mostly {{cvt|10–20|mm}} wide and arranged singly on short side shoots. The [[Hypanthium|floral cup]] is [[Sessility (botany)|sessile]], {{cvt|2.5–4|mm}} long and glabrous. The [[sepal]]s are also glabrous, {{cvt|2–3|mm}} long, the five petals {{cvt|3–7|mm}} long and the [[stamen]]s {{cvt|3–4|mm}} long. Flowering mostly occurs from March to April and the fruit is a [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]] mostly {{cvt|8–12|mm}} wide that remain on the plant at maturity.<ref name="RBGS" /><ref name="Telopea">{{cite journal |last1=Thompson |first1=Joy |title=A revision of the genus ''Leptospermum'' (Myrtaceae) |journal=Telopea |date=1989 |volume=3 |issue=3 |pages=421–422|doi=10.7751/telopea19894902 }}</ref><ref name="anbg">{{cite web|url=http://www.anbg.gov.au/gnp/gnp7/leptospermum-squarrosum.html|title=''Leptospermum squarrosum''|date=16 Dec 2003|publisher=Australian National Botanic Gardens|accessdate=2009-04-28}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.friendsoflanecovenationalpark.org.au/Flowering/Flowers/Leptospermum_squarrosum.htm|title=''Leptospermum squarrosum''|publisher=Friends of Lane Cove National Park|accessdate=2009-04-28}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Leptospermum squarrosum'' was first formally described in 1788 by [[Joseph Gaertner]] in his book ''[[De Fructibus et Seminibus Plantarum]]'' from specimens collected by [[Joseph Banks]].<ref name=APNI>{{cite web|title=''Leptospermum squarrosum''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/528754 |publisher=APNI|accessdate=11 June 2020}}</ref><ref name="Gaertn.">{{cite book |last1=Gaertner |first1=Joseph |title=De Fructibus et Seminibus Plantarum |date=1788 |volume=1788 v.1 |publisher=Sumtibus Auctoris, Typis Academiae Carolinae |location=Stuttgart |page=174 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/114363#page/372/mode/1up |accessdate=11 June 2020}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
Peach blossom tea-tree grows in shrubland on sandstone soils in coastal areas and nearby tablelands of New South Wales, but especially in the Sydney region.<ref name="RBGS" /><ref name="Telopea" />

==Use in horticulture==
This tea-tree is a hardy shrub that grows best in a sunny situation in well-drained soil, but is salt-resistant and tolerates exposed positions.<ref name="anbg" />
